summary: Jira Data Center: one username and password form at login.jsp on the instance's own origin. Releases from 10.2 serve a new form, older releases and legacy mode the classic one; each step lists the ids of both. Jira Cloud is not covered.

sources.title: Atlassian Data Center App Performance Toolkit 8.10.4, Selenium locators of the Jira login page
sources.note: Atlassian's own test toolkit, not Jira's source. Its README lists the supported Jira releases as 10.3.15 and 11.3.1. app/selenium_ui/jira/pages/pages.py lines 31-66 open login.jsp, use the classic ids when login-form-submit is present and the others otherwise, type both values and click. app/jira.yml line 12 documents a /jira context path.

sources.title: Atlassian jira-actions 3.28.2, login page object for the classic form
sources.note: Atlassian's own WebDriver actions. WebJira.kt line 19 opens login.jsp.

sources.title: Jira Software 10.3.x upgrade notes: new login experience with two-step verification since 10.2, and the legacy mode property
sources.note: Names the system property atlassian.authentication.legacy.mode=true, which brings the classic form back. No markup.

fixtures.note: The form of 10.2 and later: three ids. The form element, its method, the control tags and the type attributes are not in the source.
The classic form: the ids and the two field names inside the element with id login-form. Its method, the tag of the submit control and the type attributes are not in the sources.

staysInteractive.note: Two-step verification, since Jira 10.2: the code is asked after the password. The toolkit does not handle that step, so its fields are not known and no challenge is written.
Jira Cloud. No source for its sign-in was read and the profile has no hosted login URL to capture, so a Cloud site is a layout mismatch and nothing is typed.

unverified: All six ids: they come from Atlassian's test tooling, not from Jira's source or a saved page.

Whether the 10.2 form stays on login.jsp after a redirect, and whether either form is an ordinary POST form. The steps use the click submission; a form without a POST action would need the spa submission.
The login form shown on the dashboard to a signed-out visitor, and any release older than the classic form these tools target.
Single sign-on, CAPTCHA after failed attempts and other administrator options: nothing about them was read.
neededFromUser: Your Jira login page saved as "Webpage, Complete" with the Jira version, or one successful sign-in with this layout. For Jira Cloud, say so: it needs its own profile. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
schemaGaps: A path gate for login.jsp under any context path (/login.jsp, /jira/login.jsp, /anything/login.jsp) cannot be written: paths are exact and prefixes are directories. The steps therefore carry no path gate and rely on the ids.
notes: Versions: the toolkit supports Jira Data Center 10.3.15 and 11.3.1 and still carries the classic ids for instances running in legacy mode. The two tools agree on the classic form (login-form, os_username, os_password, login-form-submit).
